quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep driving at your current speed.
You must stop ahead.
Speeding is not allowed.
A traffic signal is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A traffic signal is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is ahead.

questions.question: What drugs can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold medicine
All of these

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these
questions.explanation: Many drugs can affect your driving. This includes illegal drugs and legal medicines you can buy or get from a doctor. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
A divided highway starts. Slow down to 35 mph.
Merge ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
Winding road ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road will curve to the right. Slow down to the speed shown on the sign—35 mph.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you feel tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes. Stop on the shoulder only in emergencies. Avoid using cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather. Change lanes only when necessary.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gas?

options.text: Running your car in the driveway
Accelerating quickly
Slowing down gradually
Braking hard

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down gradually
questions.explanation: Every hard stop wastes fuel because you have to accelerate again. When you look ahead and slow down gradually, you avoid sudden braking and use less gas.

questions.question: How should small children ride in a vehicle?

options.text: Held safely by a strong adult
Standing on the floor in the back
They won't get hurt because they are small
Never standing—always in a proper seat

questions.correctAnswerText: Never standing—always in a proper seat
questions.explanation: Use special child seats for small children. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during a crash or sudden stop. Children must always be secured in a proper seat.

questions.question: If an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Follow the traffic light.
Follow the officer's directions.
Honk at the officer.
Do what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: When a police officer is directing traffic, follow their directions instead of the traffic light. Officers direct traffic to help prevent crashes and keep traffic moving.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a curve or hill because you probably won't see oncoming cars
By driving on the highway shoulder
If a solid yellow line is next to you and the passing lane is clear
None of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above
questions.explanation: Do not pass on curves or hills—you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never drive on the shoulder to pass. Do not cross a solid yellow line. Only pass in safe, legal areas.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving at night
When driving on slippery roads
When driving at high speeds
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Keep a three-second distance behind the car ahead under normal conditions. Add one more second for each bad condition—such as night driving, slippery roads, or high speeds.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at the same time at a four-way stop sign, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right
The driver on the left
One driver can go without stopping
One driver should honk to give up their right-of-way

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if you arrive at the same time as another driver, the driver on your right has the right-of-way. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When driving slowly blocks the normal flow of traffic
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone
Only when driving in rural areas
When driving in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving slowly blocks the normal flow of traffic
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you block traffic flow. You can get a ticket for driving too slowly.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you and them
Brake hard to make them back off
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass
Ignore them

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors often to see if a driver is tailgating or trying to pass. If someone is following too closely, slow down and let them pass. Most rear-end accidents happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Has the right-of-way
Must yield to drivers already on the public road
May force their way into traffic
Can assume other drivers will make room

questions.correctAnswerText: Must yield to drivers already on the public road
questions.explanation: If you are entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely when you have an opportunity.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn cars
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers
Drive out fast to blend with traffic
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and roadway traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and roadway traffic
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Keep right
Keep left
Pass with caution
No passing

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway is coming. The road splits into two one-way roads separated by a divider. You must stay to the right.

questions.question: If you have a tire blowout:

options.text: Take your foot off the gas
Do not brake right away
Slow down gradually and pull off the road
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, take your foot off the gas and do not brake immediately. Slow down gradually, then gently apply brakes and pull off the road.

questions.question: Highway signs that tell you about hazardous conditions are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs
Warning signs
Information signs
Guide signs

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning signs
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to dangerous conditions ahead. Follow warning signs for your safety. Ignoring them could cause an accident.

questions.question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead
You can return to your lane before oncoming traffic reaches you
Your vehicle has enough speed to pass
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless you can see the road ahead clearly, you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle can pass at the needed speed. Do not pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: Keeping space between your vehicle and others around you is important because it:

options.text: Prevents distractions from other vehicles
Gives you time to react to unexpected situations
Keeps traffic moving at a safe speed
Keeps other drivers alert

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react to unexpected situations
questions.explanation: Leave plenty of space between your vehicle and others around you. This is the only way to be sure you have enough time to react to what other drivers do.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you are driving. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the engine
Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself
Steer with effort, reduce speed, drive to a safe area, and stop
Brake hard

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer with effort, reduce speed, drive to a safe area, and stop
questions.explanation: If your power steering stops working, you will need to steer harder to keep control. Reduce your speed and pull off the road to stop safely.

questions.question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what should you do?

options.text: You can still turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
You cannot turn anymore and must go straight.
You still have the right to turn.
You no longer need to turn in the arrow's direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can still turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in the arrow's direction. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A steady yellow light means what color light will come next?

options.text: Flashing yellow
Steady green
Steady red
Flashing red

questions.correctAnswerText: Steady red
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light will appear next.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave to tell the emergency vehicle to pass.
Move into the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Always yield to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren. Drive to the right side of the road immediately and stop. If you are in an intersection, finish crossing first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: What do orange road signs mean?

options.text: Work zone ahead.
Traffic laws apply here.
School zone ahead.
Directions to locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn drivers about work zones. These diamond-shaped signs have black letters or symbols and tell you that workers are on or near the highway.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to pedestrians:

options.text: Even if the pedestrian is not being careful.
Only when the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on your side of the road.
Only if the pedestrian signals you to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian is not being careful.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they are crossing against the light or are being careless.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs tell you?

options.text: How fast you could drive in the area
The fastest or slowest speed allowed by law
How fast to drive in heavy traffic
How fast to drive in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest speed allowed by law
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the highest and lowest speeds allowed on that road. These limits are for good conditions. You must drive slower when conditions are bad.

questions.question: You need more space in front of your car when stopping:

options.text: On a hill going upward.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll booth.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a hill going upward.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your car when stopped on an uphill slope. If the car ahead rolls backward when traffic starts moving, the extra space helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: You should be careful when passing a cyclist because:

options.text: You are moving faster.
The cyclist always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pass.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.
questions.explanation: Be careful passing cyclists because they may suddenly swerve into traffic to avoid objects in the road. Always drive carefully near bicycles.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Take a different route.
You must stop and wait for a worker.
The road is closed.
Road work is happening ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road work is happening ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange work zone signs warn you of construction or road repair ahead. Slow down and drive carefully when you see this sign.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Turn right only after a complete stop.
Do not turn right.
Left turns are allowed.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not turn right.
questions.explanation: This is a traffic law sign that you must obey. Right turns are not allowed where this sign is posted.

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from specific lanes. What does a solid red arrow mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a red circular traffic light.
Drivers may turn in the direction the arrow points.
Traffic in that direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a red circular traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red circular light. Drivers must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and a slash through it mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
An action is not allowed.
Some drivers must yield to other drivers.
Drivers should go slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: An action is not allowed.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash means something is forbidden. These signs are white with red and black markings. The red circle and slash over a symbol means that action is not permitted.

questions.question: If you get stuck in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Leave your car and go find help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk onto the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car so people can find you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car so people can find you.
questions.explanation: If you get stuck in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found if you stay with your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm is dangerous.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver who arrived first.
The driver who arrived last.
One driver should go without stopping.
One driver should wave others ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrived first.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, all traffic must stop. The first vehicle to reach the intersection goes first. If two cars arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: When there is a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, with the broken line next to your lane, when can you pass?

options.text: Only in an emergency.
Only on an expressway.
If traffic ahead is clear.
Only at an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: If traffic ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: When the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may cross it to pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Before you start the engine, what should you check?

options.text: Only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
All passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: All passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before starting the engine, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on which of these factors?

options.text: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
Whether there is a stop sign.
Whether you use your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need depends on road conditions, weather, and how much traffic is coming toward you.

questions.question: How should you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, yield to other traffic, and match the speed of traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly so you can watch the traffic.
Always stop completely first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to other traffic, and match the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: Signal before entering and match the speed of traffic already on the freeway. Always yield to other traffic when merging.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Bicycles cross here.
Stop only if other cars are coming.
Bicycle store nearby.
Soft road shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycles cross here.
questions.explanation: This sign shows where bicycles cross or ride. Drive carefully in this area because bicycles regularly cross or ride beside traffic.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing without traffic signals?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals so this will never happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When approaching an unmarked railroad crossing, slow down and be ready to stop. Look both ways on all tracks to make sure no trains are coming. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance and wait for it to pass before crossing.
